title: Transport Songs and Rhymes
strapline: Wheels going round, boats rowing, trains at the station — songs everybody can already half sing.
intent: Children develop rhythm, memory and language through songs they can join immediately.
Familiar songs give a child with less language a way to take a full part.
Actions and props connect the words to movement, which fixes them in memory.
Repeated refrains build the phonological awareness that early reading rests on.
Singing together builds confidence and a strong sense of the group.
implementation: Sing rhymes children mostly know — "The Wheels on the Bus", "Row, Row, Row Your Boat", "Down at the Station".
Add actions to every verse so children join in physically before they join in vocally.
Provide props — a steering wheel, scarves, an oar, a whistle — for children to hold.
Let children invent new verses: what else goes round and round on the bus?
Vary volume and speed deliberately — very quiet, very fast — to keep attention.
Repeat the same core songs across the half-term so children truly own them.
Praise every attempt at joining in, including humming and actions without words.
key_questions: What else could go round and round on our bus?
Can you sing it very quietly? Now very loudly?
What sound does the train make? Can we put it in the song?
Which is your favourite song? Shall we sing that one next?
Can you remember what comes after this bit?

impact.text: Children own a wide repertoire of songs and rhymes and use them in play.
Children sing familiar songs from memory, sometimes to themselves.
Children learn new songs quickly and experiment with rhythm and volume.
Children join in rhyming games and notice rhythm and syllables.
Children sing, move and perform with growing confidence.
Children grow in confidence contributing an idea to the group.

enhancements: A song-choice board with a picture for each song so children can pick.
A recorded version of the children singing, played back at tidy-up time.
An instrument basket so the songs can be accompanied as well as sung.
A prop box built up over the half-term with the children's suggestions.
A new verse book where children's invented verses are scribed and kept.
A link to the small world transport play so the songs turn up in free play.

playing_exploring: Children join in at whatever level they can — actions, humming or full song.
Props invite children to play with the song rather than just perform it.
active_learning: Children hold attention across a whole group session and come back for more.
Repetition across the half-term builds real mastery they are proud of.
creating_thinking: Children invent new verses, which is genuine creative composition.
They anticipate what comes next and notice when it is wrong.
